original_observation.message: concurrent large results should queue behind the blocked bulk writer: Elapsed(())

verified_source_chain.finding: The fixture starts129 delegates, separately waits up to10seconds for started>=129, releases them, then waits up to10seconds for bulk_rx.len()>=129 without consuming bulk frames. The actual panic is the second wait, so the first start barrier was reached. The later unrelated-cell start, per-frame decode/size checks and final alive assertion were not reached.

Each started delegate returns a256KiB string after the same release token is cancelled. This is129 payloads,33,816,576bytes (32.25MiB) before framing, on an in-process channel fixture; no real provider or network host is used.
MAX_PENDING_DELEGATE_CALLS is1024; the bulk mpsc capacity is that constant. The intended129 queued responses do not statically fill this queue. It is not a128-slot overflow.

Each callback task is awaited by a completion forwarder, which sends DelegateCompleted through the16-slot event channel. The driver drains this channel and processes results; senders do not need bulk_rx to consume before the129 expected frames fit.
The driver synchronously encodes each completed result and try_sends it on the selected lane. Full/closed bulk queues cause fail(), rather than an asynchronous wait on bulk capacity.
Tool-result DelegateResponse messages select Bulk; only notification acknowledgements and control requests use Control.
The encoded per-frame limit is64MiB. The intended256KiB result is not statically beyond this limit. This source check is not an observed serialization-time measurement.
The driver selects cancellation first, drains events and forwards result frames; fail marks alive=false, records the first reason, fails requests, cancels delegates and cancels the lifecycle.
DriverHarness Drop requests cancellation; it does not await driver_task. On this panic the fixture unwinds. The raw does not record joined cleanup or active-task counts.
